title: When Darkness Falls and Night Is Here
description: When Darkness Falls and Night Is Here in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900), headed “Synesius”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When dark-ness falls and night is here, My hymns of praise in si-lence rise This knows the moon, whose sil-ver sphere Shines in the star be-span-gled skies.

lines: When darkness falls and night is here,
My hymns of praise in silence rise —
This knows the moon, whose silver sphere
When morning breaks, and glorious day
Shines in the dawn and noontide fair —
This knows the sun — a grateful lay
Springs from my heart in fervent prayer.
When fails the light at sunset gray,
And twilight listens for my song —
This know the stars — in bright array
My praises mingle with their throng.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
